title: Special bits not both set force disjointness
statement: Let $n \ge 1$, and let $b_x, b_y \in \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}$ be prescribed bits that are not both $\mathrm{true}$. Then every hard-distribution sample whose special coordinate carries Alice's bit $b_x$ and Bob's bit $b_y$ generates a disjoint input pair: the special-bits event for $(b_x, b_y)$ is contained in the event that Alice's set $X$ and Bob's set $Y$ are disjoint.
hypotheses_covered: prescribed special bits b_x, b_y for Alice and Bob
the two prescribed bits are not both true
replaced: A prescribed special-coordinate bit pair is disjoint exactly when it is not $(true,true)$.
